newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala bus fire death toll rises to 13.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala bus fire death toll rises to 13.

text.p: Two more burn victims died in hospitals late on Monday, bringing to 13 the death toll from an explosion and fire aboard a Guatemala City bus, firemen said on Tuesday.
"A total of five people died at the scene and eight died on the way to or in the hospital," William de Leon, spokesman for Guatemala City's volunteer fire department, told Reuters.

Among the dead in the fire was a 2-month-old infant. More than two dozen people were injured in the blaze and many had to break windows to squeeze out because they could not escape through a blocked exit door.

An iron bar soldered and screwed into place across the back door emergency exit trapped dying and injured passengers inside the bus and hampered firemen trying to rescue them, Cecilio Lopez, director of the National Guard, told reporters.
Firemen said the blaze was accidentally caused by two men who boarded the packed bus smoking cigarettes and carrying canisters of paint thinner.
In the confines of the bus, fumes from the thinner ignited and caused the explosion, firemen said.
Fourteen different private bus companies run the thousands of creaky, old and overcrowded buses that transport the majority of Guatemala's 2 million inhabitants.
Government officials and citizens on Tuesday called for stricter bus-safety rules.
